atoms.text: Before the Romans came to Britain, the Britons worshipped many gods and goddesses representing different parts of nature. The Romans had a similar belief system, although their gods had different names.

As their beliefs were alike, the Romans did not force the Britons to give up their religion. Instead, they respected local gods and often linked them with similar Roman ones, worshipping them side by side under both Celtic and Roman names.

atoms.a: What was similar about Roman and Celtic beliefs?
b: They had the same names for all gods.

atoms.a: In which two ways did the Romans treat Celtic religion?
b: ++They combined Celtic beliefs with their own religion.
They banned all Celtic ceremonies and worship.

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps in this conversation between a Briton and a Roman.

atoms.b: Do you think our ((++Celtic Christian)) gods are very different from yours?
Not at all! Your ((++god emperor)) Taranis reminds me of our god Jupiter. They both rule thunder and the sky.
I had never thought about that before! What about Belenus, our god of sun? We often ((++pray pay)) to him for help.
atoms.sound: I had never thought about that before! What about Behleenus, our god of sun? We often pray to him for help.

atoms.b: He sounds a lot like Apollo! My favourite though is your ((++goddess god)) Sulis. She watches over the hot springs, so we connect her with Minerva, our goddess of healing.
Is that why you ((++Romans Tudors)) now call her Sulis Minerva?
Exactly! We often mix our gods with your ((++local opposite)) ones instead of replacing them.

hint.label: Persecuted

atoms.b: Unlike Celtic ((++beliefs leaves)), Christianity was illegal during much of the Roman era, and Christians were persecuted.
However, it is said that in AD 312, ((++Emperor doctor)) Constantine saw a divine vision of a cross before an important battle. After his victory, he legalised Christianity.

feedback.finish: After Christianity was legalised, it began to spread more widely in Roman Britain as well as the rest of the empire.
